parent.description: Wider league this is part of, e.g. 'cfb-fcs' points at 'cfb'. Teams that move between divisions keep their slug under the parent code.

aliases.description: Other names people use, e.g. 'Premier League', 'EPL'.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, when the league is national.

ageGroup.description: Same values as team.ageGroup. Leave out for the senior game, e.g. 'under-20' for an under-20 World Cup.

category.description: What kind of competition this is, using 2nd Screen's values: 'league' has a season table (a college division such as FCS is a league with a parent), 'tournament' is a single event like a World Cup, 'series' is a season of separate events with their own results (motorsport series, golf tours), 'fixture-group' is a loose set of games like international friendlies.

discipline.description: Same values as team.discipline. Leave out for the standard game.

multiSport.description: True exactly when sport is 'multi', e.g. the Olympics.

teamPrefix.description: League code used in this league's team slugs, when it differs from the record key, e.g. 'cfb' for 'cfb-fcs'.

main.description: Record key is the league code used as the first part of every slug, e.g. 'nfl', 'cfb', 'cfb-fcs', 'f1', 'nascar', 'epl'. Lowercase a-z, 0-9 and '-'. Never reused once minted.

description: A league, tour, series or college division. Gives every league code used in team, game and leaderboard slugs a record of its own, so others can look codes up.
